title: Out-of-band Windows update fixes slmgr/KMS activation failing with 0x80041008 after the November 2026 update
summary: After the 10 November 2026 security update, some enterprise devices fail slmgr.vbs operations (KMS host configuration, product key install, licensing management) with 0x80041008 (Invalid parameter). Microsoft released out-of-band cumulative updates on 13 November 2026 (MC1551898): KB5136489 (Server 2025, OS build 26100.33828), KB5136487 (Server 2022), KB5136490 (Server 2019 / Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019), KB5136483 (Windows 11 23H2) and KB5136493 (Windows 10 22H2 ESU / Enterprise LTSC 2021). Already-activated devices stay activated.
why: The break hits automation, not end users: imaging task sequences, KMS host rebuilds, Autopilot/OSD scripts that run `slmgr /ipk` or `/skms`, and ESU MAK key installs on Windows 10 22H2. For servers and Windows 10 the fix is Catalog-only, so WSUS/ConfigMgr/Update Manager rings will not pick it up unless you import it.
todo: Search provisioning and build logs (task sequences, Arc/run-command scripts, golden-image pipelines) for 0x80041008 since 10 November.

Import the matching KB from the Microsoft Update Catalog into WSUS/ConfigMgr for KMS hosts and image build machines first; it includes the November security fixes, so it replaces rather than adds to the monthly CU.
On Windows 11 23H2 the OOB update is also offered as an optional update in Windows Update; decide whether Windows Update for Business rings should take it or wait for December.
Re-run the failed `slmgr` step and confirm with `slmgr /dlv` that the expected channel and KMS host are reported.
